basics.name: Matt L. Briselli
basics.label: Senior Technical Program Manager (L5), Software Engineer, Chemist & Production Stage Manager
basics.summary: Trained chemist (Carnegie Mellon B.S. Chemistry; Dr. Veronica Hinman Evo-Devo Biology Lab) turned Software Engineer and Senior Technical Program Manager with 8+ years at Google (currently leading Google Photos Storytelling — Recap, Memories & Video Editing in NYC; previously Photos Foundations/Ultra HDR/Locked Folder in SF and Google Maps Android Platform in Seattle/SF) and 2+ years at Adobe Federal, alongside 25+ theatrical productions as a Production Stage Manager/Director and summers as a flying trapeze catcher. Not actively searching for a job, but open to extraordinary opportunities as a Sr. Software Engineer, Sr. Technical Program Manager, or Theatre Stage Manager.

citiesLivedIn: San Francisco, CA (6 years, 3 with a Pacific Ocean bedroom view)
Shanghai, China (Summer study abroad at Shanghai International Studies University)

work.name: Google (Google Photos — Storytelling)
highlights: Responsible for the Photos Storytelling & Reminiscing Mission within Google Photos.
Builds and launches reminiscing features including the 2025 Google Photos Recap, Memories, and Video Editing across the Google Photos app and Google surfaces.

work.name: Google (Google Photos — Foundations Client, Data Processing & Video)
highlights: Led cross-PA Android (Media, Codecs, Graphics), Pixel, and Google Photos teams to launch the Ultra HDR image format in Android 14, drive ISO/TC-42 gainmap standardization, enable OEM adoption ('Super HDR'), and ship ML HDR editing tools.

Managed two teams (50 engineers) to launch Cloud-Based Locked Folder across Android, iOS, and Web, rolled out AI-powered Video Key Moments, and built an automated bug triage pipeline for Android and OEM partners.
Won the company-wide Google Healthy Award (Q1 2024) for a year-long Google Photos testing & tech-debt initiative.

work.name: Google (Google Maps — Android Platform)
work.position: Technical Program Manager II → III (L4 → L5)
highlights: Managed 30 engineers shipping the Android 12 Material You Search & Nearby Traffic homescreen widgets, and served as TPM for Android and iOS Maps Incognito Mode.
Led 100+ engineers auditing a decade-old codebase across Maps, Maps Go, and NavGo to launch Google Play Data Safety Labels.
Drove performance improvements (jank, startup/transition latency, power/thermal) and designed an integrated client-server testing framework across Maps surfaces.
Served as Google San Francisco Culture Lead (Jan 2020 – Mar 2022), managing a $160k event and grant budget.

work.name: Google (Google Maps — Android Platform / aGMM)
highlights: Won Global Google Maps Hackathon (Overall, People's Choice, Site awards) and served as Tech Lead for a 10-person iOS & Android team to launch Speakeasy Text-to-Speech place/address pronunciation in 50 languages.
Major contributing SWE on the Maps 15th Birthday UI Redux (tab-switching backstack and prefetching) and redefined traveler localization to resolve long-standing international travel bugs.
Led feature development and API reviews on a customizable caching data-layer and built a testing oversight team.

work.name: Adobe Systems Federal (Project Romeo)
work.position: Software Developer / Government Consultant & Tech Lead
highlights: Developed and configured web content management solutions using Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Sites, Forms, Assets, Communities, and Apps (Java, JSP, Sightly, JavaScript, HTML, XML).
Served as Tech Lead on Project Romeo constructing modular components emulating Microsoft Outlook (calendars, addresses, tasks). Won the Jan 2017 Sales Achievement Award.

work.name: Camp Cayuga
highlights: Worked on the board of the flying trapeze rig, caught trapeze flyers, taught and performed on lyra, and taught circus arts (juggling, diabolo, devil sticks, spinning plates).

work.name: Carnegie Mellon University — Dr. Veronica Hinman's Evolutionary & Developmental Biology Lab
work.location: Pittsburgh, PA (Mellon Institute of Industrial Research)
highlights: Performed gene knockdowns on the fully sequenced genomes of the Sea Star and Sea Urchin to observe effects on regeneration and developmental traits.

education.institution: Carnegie Mellon University (Mellon College of Science)
education.area: Chemistry (with coursework in Computer Science, Chinese, Scenic Design & Acting)
Chinese Studies (Mandarin Chinese for Oral Communication & The Structure of Chinese)
